title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. X̄ is the Artin–Verdier compactification of Spec Z, i.e. Spec Z together with the real place, with its étale site. S is a nonempty finite set of closed points (primes) and Ū = X̄ − S. The page computes the étale cohomology of G_m on Ū from the known cohomology of X̄. This continues the Brauer-group discussion of the previous page (Br(X) → Br(η) injective). The next page uses the result to get H^i(Ū, μ_{ℓ^n}), H^i(Ū, Z_ℓ(1)) and a 'rational' H^i(X, Q(1)) = Q, 0, 0, Q. So the page serves the 'arithmetic theory / Galois theory of motives' project: it computes the realizations of the Tate motive Z(1) over Z[1/S].

Step 1: excision sequence.
... → H^i_S(X̄,G_m) → H^i(X̄,G_m) → H^i(Ū,G_m) → H^{i+1}_S(X̄,G_m) → ...

Step 2: local cohomology sheaves. On a regular one-dimensional scheme we have the divisor sequence 0 → G_m → j_*G_{m,η} → ⊕_x i_{x*}Z → 0. We also have R^q j_*G_m = 0 for q ≥ 1, by Hilbert 90 and because the Brauer group of the fraction field of a strictly henselian DVR vanishes. Together these give the sheaf H^i_x(G_m) = 0, Z_x, 0 for i = 0, 1, ≥ 2.

Step 3: global local cohomology. Hence H^i_S(X̄,G_m) = H^{i-1}(S,Z) = ⊕_{x∈S} H^{i-1}(Gal(F̄_p/F_p), Z). Using 0 → Z → Q → Q/Z → 0 (written on the page) and cd(Ẑ) = 1 for torsion modules, this equals:
- 0 for i = 0;
- Z^S for i = 1;
- 0 for i = 2;
- H^2(S,Z) = H^1(S,Q/Z) = (Q/Z)^S for i = 3;
- 0 for i ≥ 4.

Step 4: known values on X̄ (class number 1 for Q, plus Artin–Verdier). H^0(X̄,G_m) = Z^* = {±1}, H^1 = Pic = 0, H^2 = Br = 0, H^3 = Q/Z, and H^i = 0 for i ≥ 4. Therefore H^i(X̄,G_m) ≅ H^i(Ū,G_m) for i ∉ {0,1,2,3}, since both vanish.

Step 5: the sequence splits into two pieces.
- Low degrees: 0 → {±1} → H^0(Ū,G_m) → Z^S → 0, and H^1(Ū,G_m) = 0. So H^0(Ū) = {±1} × Z^s, the S-units of Q.
- Middle degrees: 0 → 0 → H^2(Ū,G_m) → (Q/Z)^S → Q/Z → H^3(Ū,G_m) → 0. The map (Q/Z)^S → Q/Z is the ordinary sum of local invariants. Since S ≠ ∅ it is surjective, so H^3(Ū,G_m) = 0 (Grothendieck's '?') and H^2(Ū,G_m) = Ker(Σ). This is the reciprocity law / Brauer–Hasse–Noether for Z[1/S] in the Artin–Verdier setting.

The next page then applies the Kummer sequence and passes to the limit to get the ℓ-adic H^i(Ū, Z_ℓ(1)), with a remark that ℓ = 2 needs a small modification in degree 0.

The pattern for X̄ (degrees 0 and 3 nonzero, with H^3 = Q/Z through the sum of invariants) is the '3-manifold' Poincaré-duality picture of Spec Z.
errors: The i = 3 entry H^{i-1}(S,Z) = H^2(S,Z) equals H^1(S,Q/Z) = (Q/Z)^S, not H^2(S,Q/Z), which is 0 since cd(Ẑ) = 1 for torsion modules. The transcription reads 'H^2(S,Q/Z)'; the handwriting may actually say H^1. The value used later, (Q/Z)^S, is correct.

Vanishing of H^i(X̄,G_m) for i ≥ 4 and of H^3(Ū,G_m) needs the Artin–Verdier compactified site, with modified (Tate) cohomology at the real place. For the plain étale cohomology of Spec Z or Spec Z[1/S] there is 2-torsion in all high even degrees. The bar notation suggests Grothendieck means the compactified version, and the next page's remark about ℓ = 2 shows he is aware of the issue.
H^3(Ū,G_m) = 0 is marked '?'; it does hold given S nonempty and surjectivity of the sum map.

ideas.what: Local cohomology of G_m at closed points of a regular one-dimensional scheme: H^1_x = Z_x, else 0; hence H^i_S(X,G_m) = H^{i-1}(S,Z).
ideas.modern_name: Purity / local cohomology of G_m via the divisor sequence
ideas.where_published: Le groupe de Brauer I–III (Dix exposés), SGA 4-type local cohomology

ideas.what: Cohomology of G_m on compactified Spec Z: ±1, 0, 0, Q/Z, 0.
ideas.modern_name: Artin–Verdier duality / étale cohomology of compactified Spec of a ring of integers
ideas.usually_credited_to: Artin–Verdier (1964); Mazur (1973); Milne, Arithmetic Duality Theorems

ideas.what: Computation of H^i(Ū,G_m) for Ū = X̄ − S: S-units, Pic = 0, Br = Ker((Q/Z)^S → Q/Z), H^3 = 0.
ideas.modern_name: Cohomology of G_m on Z[1/S]; reciprocity law for Brauer groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical class field theory (Brauer–Hasse–Noether); Artin–Verdier; Milne ADT II.2

ideas.what: Using this to compute ℓ-adic and 'rational' realizations of Q(1) over Z[1/S] (next page), within the Galois theory of motives.
ideas.modern_name: Realizations of Tate motives over Z[1/S]; motivic cohomology of Spec Z
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points); Deligne–Goncharov (2005)

missed.claim: Grothendieck computes, inside his 'Galois theory of motives' notes, the cohomology of the Tate twist on Z[1/S] via Artin–Verdier compactification. This links Artin–Verdier/3-manifold duality to motivic Galois groups over Z (mixed Tate motives over Z[1/S]). The link is later made explicitly by Deligne and Deligne–Goncharov, and the 3-manifold side by Mazur. This is an early private instance of that link, not a new result.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents Grothendieck working with the Artin–Verdier compactification and Tate-twist realizations over Z[1/S] as input to motivic Galois theory, well before Deligne–Goncharov.

deep.surprise_reason: The computations are standard consequences of the divisor sequence, class field theory and Artin–Verdier duality, all in the literature by the early 1970s. The only interest is historical: they appear in the context of a motivic Galois theory over Z.
transcription_corrections: The i = 3 entry is transcribed 'H^2(S,Q/Z)'. Mathematically it should be H^1(S,Q/Z) (= H^2(S,Z)), and the handwritten exponent is ambiguous. The same applies to the term in the second long exact sequence at the bottom.
Top lines 'μ_n → G_m →^n G_m', 'H^3(X,G_m) → H^3' and 'H^i_x' are struck through in the image.
The underlined H in 'H^i_x(G_m)' denotes the local cohomology sheaf, not the group.
